decisions.decision: Headline-only duplicate of the Oct 23 Kimi issuer disclosure; no new score or future policy beyond issuer's undated progressive-cyber intent above. The 81/90.5 figures are internal xdev-bench-hard pass@3, not HLE.

The exact Cryptopolitan article body, publication date, and editorial framing were not retrieved: exact-title/site search did not return it and the frozen Google News URL could not be opened. Its key claim can be checked against issuer primary: https://www.kimi.com/en/blog/kimi-k3-1-pro reports K3.1 Pro's internal xdev-bench-hard final mitigated checkpoint at 81.0% pass@3 versus 90.5% for the same-pipeline checkpoint without cyber-data/RL filtering. The issuer describes source-code vulnerability discovery/exploit tasks in a sandbox; this is not HLE. Issuer says it aims not to release open weights that extend the absolute frontier of cyber capability and intends to progressively raise the cyber capability available in open weights. It also says it will continue appropriate controls at every training stage. This is a stated general direction, not a numeric ceiling, target, named future model, release date, binding schedule, or promised degree/pace of increase. Cryptopolitan's 'plans' framing may be based on that sentence; no specific future response/timing beyond the existing Nov 4 weight-release plan is verified. The issuer statement is a weak future-open-weight update optionality, but cyber capability is a different domain from HLE and does not establish an HLE improvement or new admission. No direct score change is established.
